source_passage: Australian operating entity of the Uber group (ridesharing/food delivery; holds Australian driver and customer PII). Subject to a major confirmed breach affecting ~1.2 million Australians (2016, concealed until Nov 2017) and a formal OAIC determination (23 Jul 2021) that Uber breached the Privacy Act, plus the global Lapsus$ 2022 compromise of internal systems the Australian operation runs on. Severe, regulator-confirmed history and high data sensitivity. CAVEAT: the research flags the Australian-HQ status as false (US/Netherlands parents); the OAIC respondents were Uber Technologies, Inc. and Uber B.V., not Rasier Pacific directly. Still ranked High as an Australian-market entity with Australian-specific incidents/regulatory action. 2016 breach: names + driver's-licence numbers of ~600k drivers and PII of ~1.2M Australians; ransom paid via bug bounty and concealed until Nov 2017 OAIC determination (23 Jul 2021): Uber Technologies Inc. and Uber B.V. found to have interfered with privacy of ~1.2M Australians; remediation orders Sep 2022 Lapsus$ breach of Uber global internal systems (MFA-fatigue on a contractor account) affecting the platform AU operations run on Parent/contracting entity: Uber B.V. (Netherlands) Ultimate parent: Uber Technologies, Inc. (USA) Sister AU entities: Uber Australia Holdings, Portier Pacific, Uber Pacific, Uber Australia Pty Ltd PwC personnel/advisory links (PwC partner Craig Heraghty a director of an AU Uber entity) — NOT confirmed as statutory auditor Delivery partner of Woolworths (Uber Eats, historical); competitor Deliveroo (exited AU Nov 2022)
